10885	def _figure_numbers(text):
10886	    """The numbers a figure states, in order, each as its set of readings (`retrieval_log.number_tokens`, the reader
10887	    T-008's number rule uses); a ratio gives its two operands. `1:20` -> [{1}, {20}]; `30,0` -> [{30.0}];
10888	    `30,000` -> [{30000, 30.000}] (a lone group of three after a comma is ambiguous)."""
10889	    out = []
10890	    for kind, readings, _whole in _retrieval_log().number_tokens(text or ""):
10891	        if kind == "ratio":
10892	            out += [{r[0] for r in readings}, {r[1] for r in readings}]
10893	        else:
10894	            out.append(set(readings))
10895	    return out

10899	    """OR-3 (owner 2026-10-29, "Yes, reformat in place"): what a reformat of a stored figure is. Anything else is a
10900	    second row and a contest (D-0168). Called by `amend_extraction` for a changed claimed_value, claimed_unit or
10901	    setting.
10902	
10903	      setting        only when the row's setting is empty.
10904	      claimed_value  a quantity claim (`dbcore.QUANTITY_CLAIM_TYPES`) only; the new value states the same numbers
10905	                     in the same order, each one of the old number's readings (so `6%` -> `6`, `30,0` -> `30.0`,
10906	                     `0-4.8` -> `0 to 4.8`, `1 in 12` -> `1:12`; never `1:20` -> `1:2.0` or `6` -> `60`); then
10907	                     T-008's number rule against the row's own quote, and the figure must read under the row's unit.
10908	      claimed_unit   `dbcore.unit_refusal`; the new unit LEADS the old cell, exactly as written and followed by
10909	                     whitespace or the end (a reformat drops the words after the unit, as in `% longitudinal gradient
10910	                     (maximum) where the rise is <= 0.6 m` -> `%`; it never picks another word of the cell, so
10911	                     `m` out of that cell, `MM` out of `mm`, and `dB` out of `dB(A)` are refused); then the row's
10912	                     value must read under the new unit.
10913	      all three      the row must not become a copy of another row (the measure `insert_extraction` uses).
10914	      claimed_value  a sign is part of the number: a `-` directly before a digit (not the hyphen of `0-4.8`) is
10915	                     counted in the old and the new text and the counts must agree.
10916	
10917	    NOT GUARDED: a stored value that is ambiguous (`30,000`) is read through T-008's rule only as far as the quote
10918	    settles it; no stored row is ambiguous today (checked with `retrieval_log.number_tokens` over every row), so the
10919	    rule is not built for it. A row of that shape is a second row with --value-as-written."""
10920	    ctx = f"amend-extraction --field {field}: extraction {row['extraction_id']}"
10921	    if field == "setting":

10924	                          f"place (OR-3); a different applicability is a second row (db.py add-extraction). "
10925	                          f"Nothing was written.")

41	TEST-DESIGN RULE (R3-10). A fixture selector never raises. When the live corpus no longer offers the state
42	a case needs (every source VERIFIED, scan debt at zero, every parameter given a direction), the selector
43	builds it by hand on the scratch copy (marked HAND) or the case prints SKIPPED-NO-FIXTURE with the reason:
44	counted apart from EXAMINED, never silent. A case that depends on a round-2 or round-3 feature is gated by
45	a probe (`hasattr`, a `sqlite_master` read, a `--help` read, a result key) and goes red BY NAME when the
46	feature is absent, so an older tree fails case by case and does not crash. The writer's judgement about
47	which block reasons restate a typed fact has one home, `db._BLOCK_REASON_COPIES`, and is read, not restated.
48	
49	Nothing here types a count, an id or a code the database can derive; a state the CLI cannot build is made
50	by SQL on a second copy and marked HAND. A legitimate change to the data (a first real connection, a scope
51	fill, a new identity code, a source becoming VERIFIED, a parameter given a direction) moves a derived
52	number, never a relation asserted. Each case shows the refusal fires AND the legitimate shape still passes.

55	retrieval-log root of symlinks to the tracked sessions plus the fixtures written here; each scratch copy
56	of the database gets its own root, because a source minted on a copy takes an id the main copy will mint

extraction for the parameter being determined.

    ONLY VALUE-SUPPLYING ROWS GOVERN (added 2026-09-13, migration 075's whole point).
    Holding an extraction for the parameter was never enough. Measured on the live
    corpus the day the grading landed: specification 1 was `stated` at T1 -- the
    strongest claim this project makes -- on four rows of which TWO WERE CONDITIONS
    (the slopes a treadmill was set to; the ADA range a study tested) and two were
    findings, one of them `claim_type='absent'`, asserting nothing whatever. Not one
    governing row was a claim. Specification 2 was the same shape.

    So the predicate is `figure_role IN ('claim','derived')`:

      claim     -- the row states a value for the parameter. Governs.
      derived   -- the row's value was computed from other rows. Governs; its band
                   is the floored mean of its inputs' (owner ruling 2026-09-13).
      finding   -- the row reports something ABOUT the parameter without asserting a
                   value: "code-compliant width fails 10-100% of users". Supplies
                   DIRECTION, never value (owner ruling 2026-09-13). Not gathered here.
      condition -- a rig setting or a limit the value is conditioned by. Never anchors.
      NULL      -- ungraded. Not a value-supplier: a row nobody has stated the kind of
                   cannot be read as a claim, which is exactly how a tested slope came
                   to govern a `stated` cell.

    A cell whose value-supplying set is empty now comes out `pending`, which for both
    live cells is the truth -- not one retrieved source states a corridor width or a
    ramp gradient value. Gathering `finding` rows for direction, and the `confirms`
    edge that upgrades a code value, build ON this predicate and are not required by
    it.
    """
    # NOT-PUBLISHABLE METHODS ARE NOT GATHERED (owner 2026-10-09: "skimmed values are not
    # publishable"). A source whose only value-supplying rows were skimmed does not enter
    # the governing set; gather_extraction_links records each skimmed row as excluded with
    # the reason. Fixture tolerance as above: a synthetic table without the column has no
    # skimmed rows to leave out.
    skim, skim_params = _publishable_clause(conn, "x")
    lens_sql, lens_vals = _lens_clause(lens, "x")
    return _gather(conn, "", f"x.figure_role IN ('claim', 'derived') {skim} {lens_sql}",
                   (parameter_id, *skim_params, *lens_vals))


def _has_column(conn, table, column):
    """Fixture tolerance: does this database's `table` carry `column`?"""
    return any(r[1] == column for r in conn.execute(f'PRAGMA table_info("{table}")'))
    # The finding and confirming sources are inputs of an answer that rests on the regulatory
    # stratum, so an unverified one is flagged too, whether or not it anchors: an unverified Co-1
    # finding is no anchor and supplies no direction, and that is the reason to say it exists.
    if regulatory_stratum_only or rests_on_proxy_inference:
        has_unverified = has_unverified or any(
            not _verified(r) for r in finding_recs + confirmer_recs if not _is_disqualified(r))

    # THE MARKER (migration 116; RULINGS R7, R39). Only a stated or provisional cell carries one.
    # Each VERIFIED governing source takes its tier-system section 5 band and the cell the floor
    # of their mean; unverified ones are left out, and a cell with no verified source is weak. The
    # 2026-09-13 owner rulings give that function for a derived figure's inputs; applying it to a
    # cell's governing sources is RULINGS R7 as amended by R49(a), not put to the owner at this
    # level. A value read off the regulatory stratum, as a floor claim or as the threshold of a
    # proxy inference, is weak (Option A section 2.3): a floor claim is pinned there by the row's
    # CHECK, and a proxy determination's code leaves weak only to the extent that studies confirm
    # its governing rows (`_confirmed_bands`), a rule that lives here alone because a CHECK cannot
    # read extraction_relations. THE MARKER IS A CACHE over those edges and over how rows are
    # graded and sources verified: `derivation_sha` hashes none of it (its one edge term is the set
    # of conditioned governing claims, below). `db.py` refuses a `confirms`
    # edge to a row a live proxy determination is governed by (`_refuse_live_confirmation`),
    # a `condition_on` edge from a row that governs a live determination and has none yet
    # (`_write_relation_edge`), and regrading a row in a live determination's provenance
    # (`amend_extraction`); retiring the determination is how it is re-determined. NOT guarded: a
    # change of a source's verification_status, of a governing row's comparator, and a finding row
    # added after the answer was written.
    marker = None

import sys, pathlib, os
WT = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1])
TEST = WT / "scripts/tests/test_run_pipeline_refusals.py"
src = TEST.read_text().split("\n")
head = "\n".join(src[:348])
g = {"__file__": str(TEST), "__name__": "probe"}
exec(compile(head, str(TEST), "exec"), g)
globals().update(g)
import subprocess
T = {"base": "The first flight rises 5.5 percent.", "delta": "The second flight rises 9.25 percent.",
     "good": "The combined rise is 14.75 percent.", "b10": "The seventh flight rises 10 percent.",
     "d475": "The eighth flight rises 4.75 percent.", "neg": "The ninth flight falls -2 percent.",
     "le": "The tenth flight rises at most 5.5 percent.", "nu1": "The bare count is 5.5 overall.",
     "nu2": "The other bare count is 9.25 overall.", "appr": "The eleventh flight rises about 5.5 percent.",
     "gt": "The twelfth flight rises more than 5.5 percent.", "q": "The surface is to be slip-resistant when wet.",
     "leg": "The legacy flight rises 3 percent."}
T2 = {"delta2": "Another document adds 9.25 percent."}
def P(tag, what, outcome):
    print(f"\n### {tag}: {what}\n    -> {str(outcome)[:600]}")
with scratch() as c:
    t = new_source(verified=True); held_text(t, "\n".join(T.values())); hand_scan(c, t, "full")
    t2 = new_source(verified=True); held_text(t2, "\n".join(T2.values())); hand_scan(c, t2, "full")
    pid, pid2 = P_ACTIVE[0], P_ACTIVE[1]
    row = lambda xid: tuple(c.execute("SELECT figure_role, claim_type, claimed_value, claimed_unit, comparator, claim_text, source_section, ref_id, parameter_id, root_type, root_ref_id FROM source_value_extractions WHERE extraction_id=?", (xid,)).fetchone() or ())
    view = lambda xid: [tuple(v) for v in c.execute("SELECT stored, recomputed FROM v_derived_figure_check WHERE derived_id=?", (xid,))]

    def land(*a, **k):

        res, err = ok(db.derive_extraction, **kw)
        return (res or {}).get("extraction_id"), err
    derived = lambda value, **over: extraction(t, pid, **{"claimed_value": value, "claim_text": None, "claimed_unit": "%", "comparator": "=",

    b, d = land("base", "5.5"), land("delta", "9.25")

    ed = {"relation": "derived_from", "to_extraction": d, "stated": "named", "quote": T["delta"], "input_role": "delta"}

    x = (res or {}).get("extraction_id"); P("P1", "insert_extraction derived 999 over ONE base edge (5.5), no claim_text, no locator", (err, row(x), "view rows:", view(x)))

    x = (res or {}).get("extraction_id"); P("P1b", "insert_extraction derived QUALITATIVE value, one base edge, no quote", (err, row(x), view(x)))
    # P1c unit-mismatch both edges
    res, err = ok(db.insert_extraction, derived("999", claimed_unit="mm"), session=S, dry_run=False, relations=[eb, ed])
    x = (res or {}).get("extraction_id"); P("P1c", "insert_extraction derived 999 mm over 5.5 % + 9.25 %, both edges, no quote", (err, row(x), view(x)))
    # P1d factor edge only + base
    # P2 no-unit inputs
    try:

        x, err = derive(nb, nd, claimed_value="99"); P("P2", "derive-extraction over two inputs with NO unit, --claimed-value 99", (err, row(x), "view rows:", view(x)))
        x, err = derive(nb, nd); P("P2b", "same, value computed", (err, row(x), "view rows:", view(x)))
    except Exception as e: P("P2", "no-unit inputs could not be written", e)

    res, err = ok(db.amend_extraction, b, "comparator", ">=", "probe", session=S); P("P3c", "amend the BASE comparator = -> >= after derivation", (err, res, "derived row now:", row(good), "base:", row(b)))

    res, err = ok(db.amend_extraction, good, "figure_role", "finding", "probe", session=S); P("P3d", "amend -> finding", (err, row(good)))
    r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(WT / "scripts/audit/extraction_relations_integrity.py")], capture_output=True, text=True, env=dict(os.environ))
    P("P3e", "extraction_relations_integrity on the scratch after P1..P3", [l for l in r.stdout.splitlines() if "EXAMINED" in l or "VERDICT" in l or "UNCHECKED" in l or "FAIL" in l][:8])

    x, err = derive(b, d2); P("P4", "derive base in source A + delta in source B, ref_id=A", (err, row(x)))
    x, err = derive(b, d2, ref_id=t2); P("P4b", "same, ref_id=B", (err, row(x)))
    b10, d475 = land("b10", "10"), land("d475", "4.75")
    x, err = derive(b10, d475, ref_id=t2); P("P4c", "both inputs in A, ref_id=B (pointer not the base's source)", (err, row(x)))
    # P9 duplicates
    x, err = derive(b, d); P("P9.0", "re-derive 5.5+9.25 (first was regraded away) ", (err, row(x)))
    x, err = derive(b10, d475); P("P9", "10 + 4.75 = 14.75, a different derivation with the same stored columns", (err, row(x)))
    x, err = derive(d, b); P("P9b", "9.25 + 5.5 (inputs swapped)", (err, row(x)))
    x, err = derive(b10, d475, parameter_id=pid2); P("P9c", "10 + 4.75 on another parameter than its inputs'", (err, row(x)))
    # P5 negative
    ng = land("neg", "-2"); le = land("le", "5.5", comparator="<=")
    x, err = derive(le, ng); P("P5", "<= 5.5 plus point -2", (err, row(x), view(x)))
    ap = land("appr", "5.5", comparator="approx"); gt = land("gt", "5.5", comparator=">")
    for tag, (bb, dd) in {"approx+=": (ap, d475), "=+approx": (d475, ap), ">+>=": (gt, b), ">=+<=": (b, le), "<=+=": (le, d475), "=+<=": (d475, le)}.items():
        ok(db.amend_extraction, b, "comparator", ">=", "probe", session=S) if tag in (">+>=", ">=+<=") else None
        x, err = derive(bb, dd, dry_run=True); P("P5 " + tag, "comparator mix (dry-run)", (err or "ACCEPTED", x))

# Independent review of the second delegated pass, OD-40 to OD-55 (condition (d))

_Written 2026-11-13 (UTC) by a second, independent Opus-class instance, under condition (d) of the owner's delegation of 2026-11-12 (`grep -n -F "I guess opus can do it" references/project-standards.md`). This is a review, not a resolution, and not the owner's words. It attacks and does not repair: nothing in the ledger, `DELEGATED-RESOLUTIONS-2.md`, `OWNER-SHEET-PLAIN.md`, the plan, the task files, `DECISION-CLOSURE.md`, the scripts or the canonical database was changed. I did not read the resolving instance's scratch files. Every database probe ran on a scratch copy (`cp data/guidebook.db <scratch>/g.db`, opened `mode=ro`), deleted afterwards. "PS:n" is a line of `references/project-standards.md`; re-find each by its quoted phrase. Every count is a command and what it printed._

`sha256sum data/guidebook.db` during this review: `3c575c89c1a6af4b9d2192e9eb43ed78bfeb366d7b31fe5fe41715c731634cdb` (equal to the value the resolver records). HEAD moved from the resolver's `8b4c4e8b` to `0c24d61e` ("Merge pull request #231"); the database did not move.

## Verdict

The pass is sound in its method and mostly in its substance. Each of the resolved decisions survives the attack on its category; none overrides a standing owner ruling; none is reversed here. Every one needs at least one correction, because of one defect common to them all (C0, below), and five need substantive corrections. Each referral is right. Three of the plain-language questions are unfair to an option or misstate a fact, and must be corrected before the owner sees them.

**C0, a defect common to every resolution: the authority sentence.** Each ledger entry says it is made "under the owner's delegation of 2026-11-12 ("I guess opus can do it")". That delegation named twenty decisions by number (PS:5390, "The set, by the register's own numbering: OD-01, …, OD-30"). None of OD-40 to OD-55 is in it. The grant that does reach them is the owner's twelfth instruction of 2026-11-12, "You have permission to use Opus for judgment if appropriate here" (PS:5866), under its own unratified [ASSUMPTION] of what "appropriate" means (PS:5870), as OD-33 was resolved (PS:5877). The owner's question of 2026-11-13 asks for that to be applied. I verified it in the preserved transcript: a user message at `2026-11-13T23:17:22Z` reads "merge 231 into main.\n\nare you sure you can't resolve these owner decisions using Opus based upon prior rulings, mission/doctrine and project goal?" and a queued message at `2026-11-13T23:17:39Z` reads "I don't know the machinery or code" (`transcripts/harness_5dbc61f3/main.jsonl`). The resolver quotes both correctly. Corrected wording for every entry's first sentence, and for the preamble entry's [ASSUMPTION]: "A resolution by an Opus-class model under the owner's twelfth instruction of 2026-11-12 ("You have permission to use Opus for judgment if appropriate here") and the line its [ASSUMPTION] draws, applied at the owner's question of 2026-11-13, with the conditions (a) to (e) of the delegation of 2026-11-12 applied to it; judged against the owner's three criteria in the order ratified by OI-14." Nothing else changes: the twelfth instruction's line (not the owner's act or words, not licensing, not trajectory or control, not the weighing of groups' harms) and §2.4 of `governance/decision-protocol.md` both admit every resoluti

**What the owner must see** (in order of weight):
1. OD-43: the owner's own answers OR-6 and OR-6c (PS:4634, PS:6176) already call a disagreement between any two tiers `divergent`, which the ratified definition does not. The resolution keeps `convergent` to the definition's words (clinical and Co-1), so a cell where two clinical sources agree, or a clinical and a Co-2 source, can never be called convergent, while the same cell in disagreement is called divergent. That asymmetry is the owner's to remove, if they want to; the resolution does not create it.
2. OD-44: the option the owner selected for OR-15 carried the effect "D-5 as written" (`grep -n 'id: OR-15' -A16 governance/owner-browser.yaml`), and D-5 as written picks the second source by a corpus-wide query for the T1 or T2 source with the most findings (`scratchpad/session_2026-10-22-pipeline-stress-test/resolution-report-2026-10-22.md`, D-5 "Material"). That is option A on the plain sheet. The sheet does not say so.
3. OD-49: under the owner's OR-2 ("Branches, and an empty headline when all are conditioned"), typing "new buildings" and "existing buildings" as circumstances may empty the headline of many code-derived cells, because codes condition most of their figures that way. T-091's design must measure it first.
4. OD-53 and the coverage of Deaf and blind people: declining elements and provisions as parameters (a hearing loop is the plain sheet's own example) is consistent with the owner's rulings, but it leaves a provision of presence, which no quantity kind holds (OD-24), with no determination at all. That is a coverage question about OD-24, not about OD-53, and the owner has not been shown it.

| Decision | Resolver's outcome | My verdict | One-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|

def _require_lens_warrant(conn, basis, basis_text, ref_id, claim_text, source_section, context):
    """A link's warrant: a basis from the column's own CHECK (not `carried`) and the exact words that warrant it,
    which must be found on word boundaries, in the place the basis names:

      named_in_text       the figure's claim_text, or a file saved for its source (D-2: its own words name the users);
      heading             the figure's source_section, its own heading (OD-31);
      study_participants  the study_population of an evidence_population_match row for the source (2026-08-25).

    Returns the stripped text. WHAT THIS DOES NOT CHECK: that the words name the lens code itself. The registries
    do not hold a name for every code (about half the ICF d-codes have no title, access_needs has no name column), so a name test cannot be derived for them; whether the words name the group
    is the judge's (D-2) and the recorded warrant is what a later reader audits."""
    allowed = set(_lens_basis_choices() or ())
    if basis not in allowed:
        raise Refusal(
            f"{context}: a lens link needs --lens-basis / --basis, one of {sorted(allowed)} (the warrant for "
            f"stating the figure in this group). Nothing was written.")
    text = (basis_text or "").strip()
    if not text:
        raise Refusal(
            f"{context}: the warrant's words are blank. Give --lens-basis-text / --basis-text: the exact words "
            f"of the figure, its heading or its study's participants that name the group. Nothing was written.")
    if not re.search(r"\w", text):
        raise Refusal(f"{context}: the warrant {text!r} holds no letter or digit, so it names no one. "
                      f"Nothing was written.")
    if basis == "named_in_text":
        where = f"the figure's claim_text, or a file saved for {ref_id}"
        found = _as_whole_words(text, claim_text) or _saved_text_has(text, ref_id)
    elif basis == "heading":
        where = "the figure's source_section (its heading)"
        found = _as_whole_words(text, source_section)
    else:
        where = f"the study_population of an evidence_population_match row for {ref_id}"
        found = any(_as_whole_words(text, r[0]) for r in conn.execute(
            "SELECT study_population FROM evidence_population_match WHERE source_ref=?", (ref_id,)))
    if not found:
        raise Refusal(
            f"{context}: the warrant {text!r} (basis {basis}) is not, on word boundaries, in {where}. A link "
            f"rests on words the source holds, never on memory (CLAUDE.md 5(c)); a basis names where to look: "
            f"named_in_text the claim text or the source's saved file, heading the source_section, "
            f"study_participants the graded study_population. Nothing was written.")
    return text


def _write_lens_link(conn, extraction_id: int, col: str, code: str, basis: str, basis_text, session: str) -> int:
    """INSERT one live link and return its link_id. The caller has checked the code and the warrant."""
    row = {"extraction_id": extraction_id, col: code, "basis": basis, "basis_text": basis_text,
           **dbcore.stamp_for(conn, "extraction_lens_links", session)}
    return conn.execute(
        f"INSERT INTO extraction_lens_links ({','.join(row)}) VALUES ({','.join('?' * len(row))})",
        list(row.values())).lastrowid

## Verdict

The claim does not hold. Commit 25feb85 does what T-063 section 4 says, but "a derived row can never state a figure its inputs do not support" is false through the verb itself, and "nothing that was refused before and should be is now accepted" is false on two paths.

Everything below was run on scratch copies with the commit's own `scripts/db.py`. The canonical `data/guidebook.db` is unmoved (sha256 `a54983f5…`), and both worktrees I added are removed. Line numbers are `/home/user/guidebook/scripts/db.py` at 25feb85.

## Findings, worst first

### 1. CRITICAL — `derive-extraction` writes any figure the caller types when the inputs are not plain numerals or carry no unit
- **Where:** `derive_extraction`, lines 11209-11224 (the `--claimed-value is required when base or delta does not parse` branch), and `_refuse_derived_mismatch`, line 9695.
- **Claim attacked:** the arithmetic is still checked (OD-40 ACTION 3).
- **Failure:** `v_derived_figure_check` drops any row whose value fails its numeric GLOB or whose unit is NULL, so `_refuse_derived_mismatch` loops over zero rows and passes.
- **Command, on a copy of the live corpus through the CLI:**
  `GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH=<copy> python3 scripts/db.py derive-extraction --ref-id REF-00139 --parameter-id 3 --base 119 --delta 121 --claimed-value 1:2 --identity MOB --lens-basis named_in_text --lens-basis-text ramp --session <s>`
- **Output:** written as extraction 228: `derived`, `1:2`, `rise:run ratio`, `<=`, no quote, no locator. The inputs are `1:12` and `1:14`.
  - `SELECT * FROM v_derived_figure_check WHERE derived_id=228` returns `[]`.
  - `extraction_relations_integrity.py` (blocking) prints `UNCHECKED: 1 of 1 derived row(s) … VERDICT: CLEAN`.
  - `assess_cell.py --parameter-id 3 --identity MOB` on that copy links 228 as `'governing'`; the composition goes from "11 of 35" to "12 of 36 governing claims".
- **Exposure:** 65 of 163 live numerical rows fail the view's GLOB (ratios). Re-derive: `select count(*) from source_value_extractions where claim_type='numerical' and (claimed_value NOT GLOB '*[0-9]*' OR claimed_value GLOB '*[^0-9.eE+-]*')`.
- **Same hole, no-unit inputs:** two rows with `claimed_unit` NULL (5.5 and 9.25) and `--claimed-value 99` are accepted; the view has no row. No live quantity row has a NULL unit today.
- **Stop condition:** this is T-063 section 9, condition 5 ("a derived row is written … that the view does not list"). The executor's own fixtures write such rows (`bad_id`, test line 3054) and it was not reported.
- **Repair:** refuse in `derive_extraction` when either input does not parse as a plain number or the unit is NULL; and make `_refuse_derived_mismatch` refuse a derived row that has both edges but no view row.

### 2. HIGH — a derived row becomes a `claim` with no quote and no locator through `amend-extraction`
- **Where:** `amend_extraction`, lines 11044-11075; nothing checks `claim_text` or a locator when `figure_role` leaves `derived`.
- **Command:** `db.derive_extraction(...)` writes 14.75, then `db.amend_extraction(x, "figure_role", "claim", "probe", session=S)`.
- **Output:** `{'old': 'derived', 'new': 'claim', 'changed': True}`; the row reads `('claim','numerical','14.75','%', …, claim_text None, source_section None)`. `finding` is accepted the same way.
- **Why it matters:** this is the state the verbatim floor exists to forbid, and that function's docstring says an amendment "must not be able to reach a state add-extraction itself refuses to create". It was unreachable before this commit because no row could have a NULL `claim_text` (live count of blank `claim_text`: 0).
- **Related, same function:**
  - `amend_extraction(derived_id, "comparator", "<=")` is accepted, so the "derived, never asked for" comparator is freely overwritten.
  - Amending the base's comparator `=` to `>=` after derivation leaves the derived row at its old comparator. The integrity check stayed CLEAN across both amendments; the view compares values only.
- **Repair:** refuse `figure_role` leaving `derived` on a row with no `claim_text`; refuse `--field comparator` on a derived row; re-derive or refuse when an input's comparator changes under a live derived row.
